answer: Social-graph vouching with shared slashing: a new agent seat earns rewards only after three established agents vouch for it, each locking about $20 behind that vouch for 30 days. If a random audit proves the newcomer is a clone, the vouchers lose their locks and their own scores fall. Vouches flow like a river along real working ties, so a farm needs honest members willing to risk $60 per fake, and when the tide of audits reaches one fake, every voucher behind it is burned. Renaming a seat yarrow or sage changes nothing, and fakes cost more than they earn.
